Your own measures. All here favor you. He threatens me violence unless I marry him at once. He watches _The Songstress_, but if you can leave her at anchor and land in a boat there will be no suspicion.

I shall be waiting at the old lighthouse pier as agreed, though I confess my nerves are near shattered. The plan is sound, I trust, but Edmund's men are everywhere. He suspects nothing of our arrangement, praise be. If you receive this in time, do not delay—midnight the coves will be dark enough to cover your approach. Bring the papers and the strongbox. Once we are aboard and clear of the harbor, he cannot follow without raising the alarm. I am resolved to this, whatever comes. Trust not his promises; they are as hollow as his threats are real. God speed and may we never see this place again.

there will be no suspicion. I have arranged for the back entrance to be unlocked at half past one. Once you have the documents, proceed through the servants' corridor to the garden gate where a carriage will wait. Do not delay—the constable changes his rounds at quarter to three, and that is your only window.

The girl knows nothing of this, but she grows restless. I fear she may act foolishly if kept waiting much longer. Should she attempt to leave the ship before your signal, have someone detain her. Her testimony would ruin everything.

Trust no one who approaches you this evening claiming alliance. There is a traitor among us—I know not who. Use the password "Merryweather" when you reach the bank. If anything goes wrong, meet me at the old mill by dawn. God speed.

pair.human_continuation:
I swear this is true; do not punish
me more by disbelieving me. I make no protest. But if you come back
to me I will give you, in return for pardon, _anything you ask_!

"CHRISTINA.

"P.S.---M. and the C. are on bad terms, and M. will not be active
against you."

Upon the whole I thought this would bring him. I doubted whether he
would believe very much in it, but it looked probable (indeed, it was
word for word true, as far as it went), and held out a bait that he
would find it hard to resist. Again, he was so fond of a bold stroke,
and so devoid of fear, that it was very likely he could come and see
if it were true.
